chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Can a man enter Makkah without iḥrām? He said: “No, except one who is ill or one who has a stomach ailment.”

key_terms.إِحْرَامٍ: iḥrām, the consecrated state required for pilgrimage rites
key_terms.بَطَنٌ: a stomach ailment or abdominal illness
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ: without, indicating absence of the required state
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city whose entry is being discussed

ai.seo_question: Can someone enter Makkah without being in iḥrām?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that entering Makkah requires iḥrām as a general rule. It also establishes an exception for a sick person or one suffering from a stomach ailment, indicating accommodation in cases of hardship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2753 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja'far (as): "Can a person enter Mecca without being in the state of ihram?"
Imam (as) said: "No, except for someone who is ill or has a stomach ailment."
